title: Committee for the Relief of the Sufferers at Mogador: List of Subscribers
purpose: Relief of the Jewish community of Mogador (Essaouira) after the French bombardment of August 1844.
notes: Printed as a “List of Subscribers to this date”. Full transcription of 263 entries from a clear scan, replacing the earlier partial draft. Gifts received through five of the banks are printed in separate sections with subtotals; the Barnett, Hoare section’s printed subtotal (£54 5s.) is 2s. less than its entries as transcribed. Total as transcribed: £2,313 9s. 6d. (no grand total is printed).

title: San Francisco Contributors Who Have Responded to the Appeal Made on Behalf of the Jewish War Sufferers in Eastern Europe
purpose: Relief of Jewish civilians in Eastern Europe during the First World War.
image_credit: Historical Jewish Press, National Library of Israel and Tel Aviv University
notes: Full transcription of all 919 entries, alphabetical as printed. Entries are San Francisco contributors unless a place is given. Spellings, including apparent misprints, are kept as printed. Amounts in the second column of the second scan sit on a curved part of the page and were matched to names by order; these are marked as probable.

title: List of Annual Subscribers to the Anglo-Jewish Press, for the year A.M. 5603
purpose: Annual subscriptions to the Anglo-Jewish press for the year 5603 (ending 24 September 1843).
image_credit: Historical Jewish Press, National Library of Israel and Tel Aviv University
notes: Full transcription, grouped by town as printed. One copy unless a number is given. Places follow the printed town headings; London addresses and other places printed after a name are kept in the name.

title: List of Subscribers to the Anglo-Jewish Press.—Vol. V.
purpose: Subscribers to the Anglo-Jewish press (The Voice of Jacob), volume V.
image_credit: Historical Jewish Press, National Library of Israel and Tel Aviv University
notes: Full transcription, grouped by place as printed (London, Liverpool, Manchester, Birmingham, then towns A–Z, Gibraltar, the West Indies, other countries and America). One copy unless a number is given. Date: the digitized copy is labelled 9 October 1845, but the imprint on the same page reads Friday, September 11, 1846, and Sir Moses Montefiore is styled Bart. (created 1846), so 11 September 1846 is used here.

title: The Jews of Brussa
purpose: Relief of the suffering Jewish community of Brussa (Bursa) following the earthquakes of 1855.
image_credit: Internet Archive, digitized from microfilm IA40607318-01
notes: All 24 donation entries transcribed from the scan. The acknowledgement is dated 16 October 1855; the issue was published on 19 October. Dublin Synagogue (£5 0s. 0d.) and Members of the Synagogue (£7 7s. 6d.) are separate entries; their printed subtotal of £12 7s. 6d. is not counted again. Only places stated or explicit in synagogue names are assigned; other donors are not assumed to live in London. Source: https://archive.org/details/sim_jewish-chronicle_the-jewish-chronicle-and-the-hebrew-observer_1855-10-19_12_44/page/n3/mode/1up

title: Melbourne New Synagogue: subscriptions toward building a new synagogue
purpose: Building a new synagogue in Melbourne large enough for the Jewish community. Subscriptions entered into at an adjourned meeting in the Vestry Room on Sunday 28 August 1853.
notes: Reprinted in The Jewish Chronicle from the Melbourne Argus of 17 September 1853. 187 subscriptions totalling £4379 10s. 0d. (as transcribed; no total is printed). Names are given as printed; 'Mr.' and 'Messrs.' apply to the indented names that follow them. The list is not in strict order of amount.

title: List of Annual Subscribers to the Anglo-Jewish Press (Vol. III, A.M. 5604)
citation: Vol. II, no. 55 (bound with Vol. III title page)
purpose: Annual subscriptions to the Anglo-Jewish press for Vol. III, A.M. 5604 (29 September 1843 – 16 September 1844).
notes: Full transcription, grouped by place as printed. One copy unless a number is given. Found at the end of the digitized issue of 15 September 1843, after the title page for Vol. III; the date of the list itself is not legible on the scan. A note at the foot says most American subscribers were left out for lack of space.

title: Manchester Hebrew Educational Society: additional donations towards the fund for building a Jewish school
purpose: Building a Jewish school in Manchester.
notes: Additional donations after an “amount previously advertised” of £794 17s. 6d. (not counted here). 134 entries totalling £524 3s. 6d. as transcribed; no total is printed. Places are given only where printed (“ditto” = the place above). Many donors are Manchester merchants and firms, not all Jewish.

title: Hebrew Congregation, Swansea: donations for the synagogue mortgage and burial ground
purpose: Paying off a mortgage on the Swansea synagogue and buying the freehold of its burial ground, described as the only Jewish burial ground in Wales.
notes: Donations already received, grouped by town as printed. 43 entries totalling £69 12s. 6d. as transcribed. Donations were received in London by Sampson Samuel and at the Jewish Chronicle office, and locally by agents in Manchester, Liverpool, Birmingham and Swansea.

title: Kahal Kados Sheerit Israel: subscriptions to buy land and build a synagogue
purpose: Buying a lot of land and building a synagogue for Congregation Shearith Israel, New York — the Mill Street synagogue, dedicated in 1730.
notes: Manuscript pledge list dated 15 Heshvan 5489 (autumn 1728). The signers undertook to pay half when the land was bought and half when building began. Benjamin Mendez Pacheco, Jacob Franks, Mordecai Gomez and (interlined) Moses Gomez were to manage the work and account for it, and give a £1,000 bond to Daniel Gomez, Abraham Isaacs and Nathan Levy on behalf of the congregation, to be recorded in the Town Clerk's office. The right-hand column is totalled £182 11s. 6d. (the entries as transcribed come to £181 11s. 6d.); Isaac Gonsales's £5 brings it to £187 11s. 6d., and later pledges were added on the left. Several names are torn or struck through.

title: Shearith Israel: memorandum of what we received of sundry people that signed on the other side
purpose: Payments received against the Mill Street synagogue pledges.
notes: Back of the pledge sheet, headed “Nov. 10” (year not legible). Running totals are written in: £56 6s., £71 10s., £87 6s. 8d., £100, £104, then Jacob Hays's £4 on 14 April. The right side lists payments made by Jacob Franks: to Mr. Nichols for drawing the writings (14s.), charges (9s.), Mr. Morison and Alderman Schuyler, a tax on the lot (2s. 10½d.), £100 to Mr. Cooper (presumably for the lot), and 18s. to Mr. Sharpas for recording — £103 5s. 10½d. in all, leaving £4 14s. 1½d. due to the synagogue. Upside down at the foot is the end of the agreement from the other side.
